---
title: "ProteoVaultR overview"
---

**ProteoVaultR is designed to help you explore and analyze SpectroMesa pipeline
results in R.** It reads the DuckDB database generated by
[ProteoVault](https://github.com/TheBoutrosLab/package-ProteoVault), bringing
identifications, quantitative measurements, and quality-control results together
for your analysis.

## 1. Why ProteoVaultR?

When a proteomics run finishes, there is still plenty to understand. How consistent
are your samples? Which proteins change between conditions? What peptide evidence
supports a result?

SpectroMesa produces the results needed to explore these questions, but they are
spread across output files from different analysis steps. ProteoVault links those
results in a single database. ProteoVaultR gives you a way to work with them in R,
so you can spend less time reading files and matching identifiers, and more time
understanding your experiment.

## 2. What can you do with it?

ProteoVaultR supports results from **SpectroMesa-DIA** and **SpectroMesa-DDA**,
including **DDA label-free (LFQ)** and **TMT** experiments. You can use it to:

- Inspect the measurements and identification evidence available in your results.
- Check sample quality through quantitative summaries and plots.
- Combine quantities with sample metadata and prepare matrices or
  `SummarizedExperiment` objects for analysis.
- Explore normalization and missing values, then compare experimental conditions
  with limma.
- Plot individual proteins and examine their supporting peptide or precursor
  measurements and sequence coverage, where available.

You choose the measurements and analysis steps that fit your experiment. The
available results depend on the SpectroMesa workflow and the data imported into
ProteoVault.

## 3. How does it fit together?

**SpectroMesa → ProteoVault DuckDB database → ProteoVaultR**

[SpectroMesa-DIA](https://github.com/TheBoutrosLab/SpectroMesa-DIA) or
[SpectroMesa-DDA](https://github.com/TheBoutrosLab/SpectroMesa-DDA) processes your
mass spectrometry data. ProteoVault gathers the resulting files into a DuckDB
database, which you open with ProteoVaultR.

You can then select and filter results before bringing them into R as tables or
quantitative matrices. ProteoVaultR opens the database read-only, so your saved
pipeline results stay unchanged as you explore them and try different analyses.

## 4. Where to begin

Start with [Installation](installation.html) to set up ProteoVaultR. Then follow
[Downloading the demo data](demo-data.html) to choose a HepG2 DIA, HepG2 DDA LFQ,
or HeLa TMT database for your first analysis.

For details about a particular function, visit the
[function reference](../reference/index.html) or open its help in R, for example
`?open_vault`.
